title: J.R.R. Tolkien - Middle-earth
use_cases: Use when crafting detailed fantasy world histories.
Implement when designing language systems for fictional races.
Configure when developing comprehensive in-game maps.
Use when outlining cultural customs to support character development.
Implement when structuring genealogy for royal lineages.
Use when compiling lyrical content such as songs and poems.
Configure when ensuring depth consistency across a fictional universe.
content:
What Tolkien documented: • Complete languages (Elvish, Dwarvish) with grammar • Thousands of years of detailed history • Geography with precise maps • Cultural customs for each race • Lineages of royal families spanning generations • Songs, poems, and myths of the world

What appeared in novels: Maybe 10% of his documentation. The depth shows through—the world feels ancient and real—but he didn't dump it all on readers.

Lesson: Document far more than you'll use. The depth you know creates confidence that shows through even when you're not explicitly explaining.
